prompt: People in all modern societies use drugs, but today’s youth are experimenting with both legal and illegal drugs, and at an increasingly early age. Some sociologists claim that parents and other members of society often set a bad example. Discuss the causes and some effects of widespread drug use by young people in modern day society.
essay:
Drug use has become a serious issue in many modern societies, particularly among young people. An increasing number of teenagers are experimenting with both legal and illegal substances at an early age. This essay will discuss some of the main causes of this problem and examine its effects on individuals and society.

One important cause of drug use among young people is the influence of parents and other adults. Teenagers often learn behaviours by observing the people around them. If parents or other role models regularly use substances, young people may consider this behaviour normal or acceptable. Another significant factor is peer pressure. Teenagers may experiment with drugs because they want to fit in with their friends or appear more mature. In addition, social media and the internet can expose young people to content that presents substance use as fashionable or harmless. Curiosity and a desire to escape academic or personal stress can also encourage some teenagers to experiment.

Widespread drug use can have several negative effects. Firstly, it can damage young people's education and future opportunities. Those who frequently use drugs may experience difficulties concentrating, lose motivation, or perform poorly at school. Secondly, substance use can negatively affect relationships with family and friends, particularly when it leads to irresponsible behaviour. More broadly, widespread drug use can increase social problems and place additional pressure on healthcare and public services.

In my opinion, preventing drug use among young people requires cooperation between parents, schools, and governments. Parents should provide positive examples and communicate openly with their children, while schools should educate students about the risks of substance use.

In conclusion, peer pressure, adult behaviour, social media, and personal difficulties are among the main causes of youth drug use. Its effects can harm education, relationships, and wider society, making prevention and early education extremely important.
